title: Refresh before the request leaves
dek: Moving the expiry check ahead of dispatch addresses the reported first-request failure after credentials expire.
footer: PR #42 · fix: refresh credentials before dispatch

sections.title: The refresh came after the send
sections.content:
The request function in client.ts already knew how to check credential expiry and refresh credentials. Its problem was the order. It awaited client.send(payload) first, then compared the credential expiry time with the current time. If credentials had expired, it awaited a refresh before returning the response.

That placed the check after the operation that needed valid credentials. Refresh was part of the request function, but it could not prepare credentials for a send that had already happened.

sections.title: The first request reached the check too late
sections.content:
The author reports that the first request after expiry failed. If you called the function after credentials expired, it attempted to send your payload before checking whether a refresh was needed. The change targets that first attempt by moving preparation ahead of dispatch.

The supplied diff confirms this ordering problem, but it does not show how send reports an authentication failure. No tests or execution results accompany the fixture. We can explain the control flow without assuming whether the failed send returned a response or threw an exception.

sections.title: Wait for refresh, then dispatch
sections.content:
The change moves the existing conditional refresh to the start of request. The complete function after the change shows the new sequence:

{{CODE:0}}

The <= comparison treats credentials as expired when their expiry time equals or precedes the current time. When that condition holds, await makes refresh finish before execution reaches the send. Otherwise, the function proceeds directly to dispatch. It still returns the response from the same send call.

The author accepts an extra clock read to avoid the initial failed request. The shown function, however, contains one Date.now() call before and after the change. This diff establishes a reordered check, not an added clock read.

Streaming requests remain a documented gap. The author says they use a separate path and need a follow-up; that path is absent from this diff. The supplied material gives no reason for deferring it and names no follow-up issue.

sections.title: Put credential preparation first
sections.content: PR #42 changes one function in client.ts: it checks expiry and awaits any required refresh before sending the payload. That order addresses the author's reported first-request failure after expiry. The change leaves the response-returning flow intact, while streaming requests still need their separate follow-up.
